summary.headline: Solara Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR384 crore and PAT 55% to INR16.3 crore, while Ibuprofen still posted a -12% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR384 crore (up 20% YoY) and EBITDA INR63.5 crore (up 10% YoY, 17% margin, up 80 bps QoQ), with PAT of INR16.3 crore (up 55% YoY), described as the highest EBITDA and PAT in 18 quarters. The base business grew 24% YoY to INR307 crore with gross margin of INR158 crore (51.3%) and EBITDA of INR72 crore, but gross margin was hit by West Asia-driven raw material and solvent cost increases, with about INR30 crore of revenue from pass-through pricing. Net debt fell about INR135 crore QoQ to about INR479 crore (roughly 1.9x annualised EBITDA), helped by about INR100 crore of rights issue call money. The Ibuprofen strategic review decision is deferred to Q2 FY27 results.

financial_highlights.change: +10% YoY in value; ~INR17-18 crore pass-through cost increase, adjusted ~54.5%
down ~INR135 crore QoQ (~22%); ~1.9x net debt/annualised EBITDA

segments.name: Base business (ex-Ibuprofen)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR307 crore (+24% YoY); gross margin 51.3% (about 54.5% ex pass-through); EBITDA INR72 crore (+8% YoY). Management targets about 25% +/-1% EBITDA margin for FY27 and 52-55% gross margin.

segments.name: Ibuprofen (commodity)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin -12% in Q1 on tactical tightness in solvent-constrained supply and higher prices; management guides to an EBITDA loss of INR10-15 crore per quarter on average. Strategic review outcome expected by H1 FY27 / Q2 results.

guidance_outlook: Base business EBITDA margin about 25% +/-1% for FY27 (CFO, answering Gautami Agarwal).
Gross margin range 50-55% (CEO), with base business margin 52-55% depending on product mix.
Base business growth at least 10% YoY, currently running slightly higher; FY27 outlook referenced as about 10% growth (mostly base business).
Net debt to fall to about INR440 crore by end-March 2027 (about 1.7x annualised Q1 EBITDA); net-debt-free target by FY29.
FY27 capex committed at about INR55-60 crore (about INR40 crore debottlenecking, INR10-15 crore maintenance); about INR40-50 crore per year in FY28 and FY29.
Ibuprofen strategic review decision to come with Q2 FY27 results (September); management said solution expected in H1.
capex_capacity: Base business sites (Cuddalore, Bangalore, Ambernath) average capacity utilisation about 70%.
Debottlenecking capex on high-margin product lines, aiming to expand those lines by 20-30%, with payback targeted within 2-3 quarters.
Greenfield capex not planned; Vizag facility remains mothballed. Plan to retrofit Vizag for CRAMS is on hold pending Q2 decision on Ibuprofen, Pondicherry and CRAMS demerger options.
Replacement of old reactors expected to lift operating days and absolute output.
demand_pricing: Customers have largely accepted price increases tied to solvent and raw material cost increases; some customers have resisted. Management says it is fairly confident of maintaining absolute gross margin value.
Q1 is seasonally softer for API offtake; QoQ revenue looks flat ex pass-through, management prefers YoY comparison.
Base business revenue: Q1 FY26 ~INR248 crore, Q2 FY26 ~INR240 crore, Q3 FY26 ~INR245 crore, Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 above INR300 crore.
Growth drivers: new geographies and new business wins, plus debottlenecking that raised volumes in high-margin products.
Ibuprofen: Q1 volumes were hit by solvent shortage; prices rose; management does not see a long-term strategic view on pricing given commodity dynamics and other Indian producers.
US tariff announcement: intent only, no legal framework or product scope clarified yet.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin volatility in the base business and how much of revenue growth is volume vs price?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: about INR30 crore of consolidated revenue came from incremental cost pass-through; base business gross margin 51.3%, about 54.5% adjusted. CEO cited quarterly gross margins of 53% (Q2 FY26), 55% (Q3), 54% (Q4) and 52% (Q1 FY27).

qa_highlights.question: Ibuprofen capital deployed and outlook for profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Deployed capital about INR700 crore including debt and equity. Management expects an Ibuprofen EBITDA loss of INR10-15 crore per quarter on average, with Q1 benefiting from tactical supply tightness.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Ibuprofen decision still on track for Q2 and what are the options?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO: decision expected in H1 and to be addressed in September; CFO: full capital recovery is unlikely and the cutoff or write-down will be clarified with Q2 results.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt-free target and capital allocation for FY27-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt-free by FY29, with gross debt still on the books; capex about INR40-50 crore a year from FY28, focused on debottlenecking rather than greenfield.

qa_highlights.question: Base business growth sustainability and margin range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of at least 10% YoY growth and is running higher; gross margin 52-55%; CEO declined a 5-year outlook.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cash flow and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital efficiency to be maintained as revenue grows; S&OP measures aimed at lowering inventory norms. The company does not yet call the turnaround complete, citing the need for 3-4 quarters of consistent growth.

risks_watch: West Asia crisis: raw material and solvent shortages intermittently shut lines; pass-through to customers is not complete.
Ibuprofen: strategic review outcome, possible capital write-down (full recovery of ~INR700 crore deployed is not expected), and Vizag/Pondicherry/CRAMS decisions due Q2.
US tariff framework unclear; product scope (formulations vs APIs) unknown.
Gross margin may stay below 55% if costs are not fully passed through.
Deleveraging: achieving net debt ~INR440 crore by March 2027 depends on scheduled repayments.
summary.management_tone: Confident on base business growth and deleveraging, but cautious and often evasive on forward outlook, citing a dynamic environment. Management declined a 5-year outlook and avoided precise Ibuprofen decisions, deferring them to Q2 results.
key_quotes: This is the highest EBITDA and PAT that we have achieved in the last 18 quarters.
We are comfortable with the 50% to 55% range. Of course, the aspiration is to try and get as close to 55% as possible.
So we are fairly confident of growing this business by at least 10% year-on-year kind of number.
Ibuprofen is a commodity business, right. The margins can never compare to what we have in the base business, right.

adds.what: Debottlenecking on high-margin product lines, aiming to expand those lines by 20-30%
Replacement of old reactors (lifts operating days and output; no size given)

growth.why: Management is fairly confident of at least 10% YoY base-business growth in FY27 (running slightly higher), backed by debottlenecking of high-margin lines (~INR40 cr, 20-30% line expansion), new geographies/wins and pass-through pricing, though no firm order book or new capacity numbers were given and Vizag stays mothballed with greenfield capex ruled out.
